item.text: {"summary":"An annual or biennial herb found in the Middle East, bull mallow has a hairy, upright stem. Its pinkish to light purple flowers grow where the leaves meet the stem, followed by disc-shaped, segmented fruit. The leaves and stems are eaten, often chopped and fried with olive oil, onions and spices, and historically fed besieged Jewish settlers during the 1948 Battle for Jerusalem.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"Leaves and stems are eaten, including fried as garnish or cooked like spinach; they fed besieged Jewish settlers in Jerusalem in 1948.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p2","s1:p3","s1:p5"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p5"]}}
